source: DISCOVERY-PIPELINE-PLAN.md section 12, expected calibration table; P2 sizes and thresholds from hybrid/math/profile.py

k1.model: two-layer softmax-attention model, written as two rounds of weighted retrieval over stored pairs

expected_cost.state_growth: linear in n (2 L d n words)

k1.expected_limit: fixed depth: no robust Dyck-2 or parity as n grows (plan section 21.1, Hahn 2020; TC0 bound)
k1.notes: Nesting passes because the number of rounds may grow with the listed depth (plan section 12, RASP Dyck-k construction).

k2.model: LSTM, written as a running store regulated by multiplicative switches
k2.expected_limit: copy beyond the state's bits (Jelassi et al. 2024, Theorem 2.7); finite precision
k2.notes: Copy and recall pass because the store width is chosen for the listed sizes (L log2 D and K log2 V below the state bits).

k3.model: HMM with k = 16 states, decoded to one latent state per token

expected_cost.state_growth: fixed (one state index, log2 k bits)

k3.expected_limit: finite state: Dyck-2 at depth D needs at least 2^D states
k3.notes: The plan names nesting and composition; copy and recall also fail at the listed sizes because 16 states hold 4 bits and the listed sizes need at least 16 (copy L = 8 over 4 symbols) and 32 (recall K = 8 over 16 values). Decoding to one latent state per token makes the capacity exactly log2 k bits, the assumption behind the plan's limit column; a filtering belief over 16 states would carry real numbers and leave the expected failures undefined.

k4.model: n-gram of order c = 3, written as continuation counts over the last two symbols

expected_cost.state_growth: fixed (the last c - 1 symbols); the V^c table is a corpus-scale store fixed after training

k4.expected_limit: window c: nothing beyond the last c - 1 symbols
k4.notes: Plan section 12: fails P2 on nesting and composition (and copy and recall).
